key_insight: Scaling a test-time verifier (a scorer/reranker that checks candidate action trajectories) reduces the instruction→action misalignment more effectively and efficiently than continuing to scale the policy model itself.
problem_solved: Shrinks the 'intention-action gap' in Vision–Language–Action models by providing a compute-efficient, test-time mechanism to detect and correct actions that don't match natural-language instructions.
method: Characterize test-time scaling laws for embodied instruction following to compare how performance improves with increased verifier vs policy compute/size.
Use a two-stage pipeline: a base policy generates candidate action trajectories; a larger multimodal verifier scores/reranks or filters those candidates at test time.
Empirically evaluate alignment, compute-efficiency, and robustness across embodied instruction-following benchmarks to show verifier scaling outperforms policy scaling.
impact: Practitioners can allocate compute to test-time verification to achieve stronger alignment and safer behavior without retraining or massively scaling policies, enabling more reliable deployment of embodied agents.
visual_elements: Scaling-law chart: performance (alignment accuracy) vs model size/compute comparing policy-scaling and verifier-scaling curves.
Pipeline diagram: instruction → policy generates candidates → verifier scores/reranks → selected action (with icons for robot and magnifying glass).
Before/after example: instruction + environment snapshots showing a misaligned action from the base policy and the corrected action after verification.
Cost-effectiveness bar chart: compute cost vs alignment gain for policy scaling vs verifier scaling.
paper_title: Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment
paper_authors: Jacky Kwok, Xilun Zhang, Mengdi Xu, Yuejiang Liu, Azalia Mirhoseini
